label: Mimosa A5-360 14 dBi Access Point (A5-360-14)
description: Mimosa A5 360-degree 5 GHz PTMP access point, 14 dBi omni: 2x2:2 up to 1.0 Gbps IP (1.7 Gbps PHY), 100 clients. 1x 1G RJ45 with 802.3at or passive PoE-in.
notes: Vendor figures from the A5 datasheet: **Gigabit Ethernet 10/100/1000-BASE-T**, powered by **802.3at or passive PoE (48-56 V)**, **max throughput 1.0 Gbps IP (1.7 Gbps PHY)**, **100 clients**, 14 dBi 360-degree omni. The A5c in the catalogue is the connectorized sibling - same radio, external antennas.

label: Mimosa A5x Connectorised 4.9-6.4 GHz Access Point
description: Mimosa A5x connectorised PTMP access point, 4.9-6.4 GHz with external antennas. 1x 1G RJ45 with passive PoE-in (24-56 V).
notes: Vendor figures from the A5x datasheet: **Gigabit Ethernet 10/100/1000-BASE-T**, **passive PoE 24-56 VDC** (injector not included), **4.9-6.4 GHz** coverage - the extended band is the reason to pick the x over the integrated A5-360, and it needs **external antennas**, so the radio link in a diagram depends on an antenna that is not in the box.

label: Mimosa A6 8x8 6 GHz PTMP Access Point
description: Mimosa A6 carrier-grade 6 GHz PTMP access point, 8x8 beamforming, up to 4.53 Gbps IP aggregate. 1x 1G RJ45 with PoE-in plus 2x 10G SFP+.
notes: Vendor figures from the A6 datasheet: **1 x GbE copper PoE, 2 x 10GbE SFP+ (optical, MM or SM)**, passive PoE **48-56 VDC @ 1200 mA** or a separate DC inlet, **8x8 beamforming**, **up to 4.53 Gbps IP aggregate**. The **internal switch is the useful part: two 10G cages on an access point** mean a sector can be backhauled and daisy-chained without an external switch in the tower box.

label: Mimosa C5 Integrated CPE
description: Mimosa C5 integrated subscriber CPE, 2x2:2 up to 256-QAM, 20 dBi. 1x 1G RJ45 with passive PoE-in (48-56 V).
notes: Vendor figures from the C5 datasheet: **Gigabit Ethernet 10/100/1000-BASE-T**, **passive PoE 48-56 V** (injector sold separately), 2x2:2 MIMO OFDM up to 256-QAM, **20 dBi** integrated. **48 V passive, not 802.3af**: a standard PoE switch will not power it, which is the single most common installation mistake with this radio.

label: Mimosa C5x Modular Radio (N5-X antennas)
description: Mimosa C5x modular PtP/PtMP radio, 700 Mbps IP (866 PHY), takes N5-X series antennas. 1x 1G RJ45 with passive PoE-in (24-56 V).
notes: Vendor figures from the C5x datasheet: **1 gigabit Ethernet port 10/100/1000**, **passive PoE 24-56 VDC**, **max throughput 700 Mbps IP (866 PHY)**. The radio is **modular**: the antenna is a separate N5-X part (8/12/16/20/25/30 dBi), so the same spec covers a 700 Mbps backhaul and a subscriber link - the antenna is what changes.

label: Mimosa C5x IP67 Radio (100-00101)
description: Mimosa C5x IP67 modular radio, 700 Mbps IP (866 PHY), takes N5-X antennas. 1x 1G RJ45 with passive PoE-in (24-56 V).
notes: The **IP67 variant of the C5x** (SKU 100-00101), same ports and radio as `mimosa/c5x`: **1 x gigabit Ethernet, passive PoE 24-56 V, 700 Mbps IP (866 PHY)**. Recorded separately because the enclosure rating is the purchasing decision outdoors, and a catalogue that only lists the base C5x cannot answer "which one goes on a mast".

label: Mimosa C6x OFDMA PtP/PtMP Radio
description: Mimosa C6x OFDMA radio: 2.0 Gbps IP PtP / 1.75 Gbps IP PtMP aggregate (2402 Mbps PHY). 1x 1G RJ45 with passive PoE-in (24 V).
notes: Vendor figures from the C6x datasheet: **Gigabit Ethernet 10/100/1000-BASE-T**, **passive PoE 24 V** (injector not included), **PTP 2.0 Gbps IP aggregate / PTMP 1.75 Gbps IP aggregate (2402 Mbps PHY)**. **The radio outruns its own port**: 1.75 Gbps of airside throughput behind a single 1G copper link, so the wire is the ceiling in PtP use - a detail the datasheet states and the model keeps.

label: Mimosa Gigabit Network Interface Device (NID)
description: Passive gigabit network interface device: in-line ESD and surge protection for outdoor radio installs, 2x 1G RJ-45, IP54, no power.
notes: Vendor figures from the NID datasheet: **Connectors: two (2) RJ-45**, **data transfer rate: gigabit rated**, **GDT surge arrestor** (10 kA impulse discharge, <1.0 pF capacitance), **IP54**, 0.13 kg. It is **passive - it takes no power and forwards nothing logically**; it exists so an outdoor radio's cable has a grounded demarcation point. Filed under `tap` because the vocabulary has no category for a passive two-port inline part: it is not tapping traffic, and a future `demarc` category would fit it better.
